At very small learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so a larger step helps.
Backing off from an unstable large learning rate restores stable convergence, as in experiment 12.
Strong L2 penalty underfits, so weakening it recovers accuracy, as in experiments 68 and 74.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty further constrains the weights and underfits.
Deeper networks are less stable at large learning rates, so adding a layer compounds the instability.
Removing a layer makes a high-learning-rate network easier to train, as in experiment 52.
Wider layers amplify the effective step size, so a large learning rate becomes more unstable.
Larger batches give less noisy gradients, which tempers instability at high learning rates.
With a small learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches leaves the model undertrained.
